summary: Intermittent 403s after IdP group sync: stale SAML session_index role cache
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 403s for users immediately after the IdP (On-prem SAML IdP) performs a group sync. Impact: Admin and write operations are blocked for some users while they can still view resources. Occurs only in Nimbus Health's private deployment (prod-us-east) and started after their nightly group-sync job.

Environment: private deployment (VPC) with SSO proxied through our identity-proxy; session cookies used are SameSite=Lax, cookie named rwd_sess. Customer performed an IdP-side role changeset at 03:40 UTC and ran group sync. Symptoms observed for ~seconds-to-minutes window: some affected users receive 403s for actions requiring newly granted roles while others (or same users after logout/login) succeed.

Observed severity: P1 due to business-impacting admin ops during business hours.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer updates group->role mapping on IdP and triggers IdP group sync.
2) User with existing browser session performs an admin API call (e.g., POST /v1/admin/projects/:id/keys).
3) Server responds 403 with rbac denial.
4) If user logs out and logs back in, call succeeds.

Repro rate: intermittent but correlated with IdP sync events.
logs:
[2026-03-10T03:41:02Z] auth:rbac deny user=uid:94e3 session_index=sess-0a7f reason='no-matching-role-after-eval' path=/v1/admin/projects/42/members status=403 request_id=aa7b2c
[2026-03-10T03:41:03Z] sso:proxy debug session_lookup key=sess-0a7f -> cache HIT ttl=18s roles=[team:viewer]
[2026-03-10T03:41:05Z] idp-notify info received user-change webhook for uid:94e3 groups=[prod-admins]
[2026-03-10T03:41:07Z] auth:rbac eval user=uid:94e3 live-lookup roles=[team:admin] result=ALLOW
investigation_notes: 03/10 05:45 UTC - Customer provided request logs and IdP group sync trace. Confirmed 403 responses followed immediately after IdP sync events.

Hypothesis: identity-proxy caches role assertions keyed by SAML session_index for performance; when IdP updates groups, existing sessions still return the cached role set until cache expiry. Because session_index is stable across IdP syncs, cached entry is not invalidated, causing stale RBAC decisions.
Validated on staging by reproducing IdP group change and triggering our session cache: reproduced 403 for active session, immediate success after manual cache eviction or full logout/login.

Cache TTL on private deployment was 60s; observed window where some requests hit cached old roles and were denied, others hit live-lookup due to cache miss and allowed. Race condition depends on request timing and distribution across proxy instances.
Checked related subsystems: no evidence of token audience mismatch or clock skew. Session cookie intact; no TLS issues.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 09:12: 'Opened with customer-provided logs and timeline. Requested reproducer and asked if they can perform logout as workaround.'
Nimbus Health (Customer) 2026-03-10 09:40: 'We only roll group changes nightly; forcing logout for all users is disruptive. Can you suggest less invasive workaround?'

Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-10 10:02: 'We can add an immediate cache eviction on receiving IdP user-change webhooks for affected user/session_index. Temporary mitigation: revoke session via Admin API for affected user(s) or instruct end-users to refresh session by re-authenticating.'
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10 11:25: 'Customer accepted targeted session revocation for affected admins as a short-term mitigation. Coordinating with Nimbus ops to get list of impacted user ids.'
Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-11 14:30: 'Created PR to add proactive eviction on identity webhooks and a feature flag to reduce session-index cache TTL in private tenants. See PR #4892.'

Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 08:10: 'Applied temporary workaround in customer tenant: lowered session cache TTL from 60s to 5s during their next scheduled sync window to minimize window of stale denial.'
resolution: Workaround applied: temporarily lowered session-index cache TTL to 5s for Nimbus Health during next IdP sync window and performed targeted session revocations for impacted admin accounts. Long-term fix merged: add cache eviction path triggered by identity-change webhooks and enable by default for private deployments. Deployment PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4892. Follow-up: monitor post-deploy and update SSO runbook to include guidance for large IdP group changes (recommendations include rolling sync approach or pre-emptive cache purge).
